data_description.self_diagnostics_enabled: Creates 14 diagnostic sensors for the companion: uptime, TX queue length, noise floor, last RSSI and SNR, TX and RX airtime, and packet counters. Off by default. These are local queries to the companion and send nothing on the mesh. The interval sets how often the sensors update (60 to 3600 seconds).
data_description.contact_discovery_mode: Entity per contact: every discovered contact gets its own entity (best for small meshes). Data only: discovered contacts are tracked as data only with no per-contact entity -- inspect them via the dropdown or the Get Discovered Contact service. Disabled: contact discovery is turned off entirely and any existing discovered contacts are cleared.

data_description.cli_console_enabled: Adds a CLI Console sensor. It records each command that you run with execute_command or execute_command_ui when record_to_console is on, and the response. It shows only command and response pairs, not the device log. Off by default. Use it with the text.meshcore_command helper and a Markdown card. The documentation has an example dashboard.
data_description.map_upload_enabled: Uploads the adverts that you receive from repeaters, room servers and sensor nodes to map.meshcore.io. Those nodes then show on the MeshCore community map. The firmware must allow private key export (`ENABLE_PRIVATE_KEY_EXPORT=1`). Without it, the integration cannot sign the uploads.
data_description.auto_cleanup_stale_contacts: When enabled, discovered contacts whose last update is older than the configured threshold are automatically removed once per day. Contacts saved to the node are always preserved.
data_description.auto_cleanup_stale_neighbors: Automatically remove neighbor entries and their sensor entities when they haven't been heard from in the configured number of days.
data_description.stale_neighbor_days: Number of days without hearing a neighbor before it is automatically removed (1–365).
data_description.consume_incoming_messages: Enabled by default. Turn off when another client, such as a phone over BLE, should retrieve queued channel and direct messages. Home Assistant keeps polling repeater status and telemetry and can still send commands. Messages delivered by the device may still appear in Home Assistant; this setting controls queue retrieval, not message visibility. Text replies to commands may also remain queued for the other client.
data_description.adaptive_poll_wait: When enabled, incoming channel messages fire as soon as RX_LOG data arrives (typically ~50ms) instead of always waiting the full 500ms. Late-arriving repeater data is delivered progressively. Disable if bots or automations depend on having all paths in the initial event.
data_description.flood_scopes: Comma-separated list of region scope names to match against incoming TC_FLOOD messages (e.g. pl-mz, pl-waw). When a match is found, rx_log_data will include a flood_scope field with the matched name. Leave empty to disable scope matching.

data_description.neighbors_enabled: Asks this repeater for its neighbour list after each successful status poll. Each neighbour gets an SNR sensor and a seen sensor. The list is paged: each page is one request, so the cost grows with the number of neighbours. Requires MeshCore firmware 1.14.0 or later.
data_description.password: Sent once to log in to the repeater. Leave blank for a repeater that grants access by ACL without a password.

Home Assistant keeps polling repeater status and telemetry and can still send commands. data_description.adaptive_poll_wait: When enabled, incoming channel messages fire as soon as RX_LOG data arrives (typically ~50ms) instead of always waiting the full 500ms. data_description.flood_scopes: Comma-separated list of region scope names to match against incoming TC_FLOOD messages (e.g. pl-mz, pl-waw). When a match is found, rx_log_data will include a flood_scope field with the matched name. Leave empty to disable scope matching.
data_description.traffic_policy: Governed (the default for new installs) gives the radio three budgets: a small flood budget (5, then 20 per hour), a direct budget for routed polls (20, then 120 per hour) and a budget for your messages. A poll that is out of budget waits; it is not counted as a failure. Legacy is the 2.x behavior, kept only for installs that already use it. It is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. After you leave Legacy, you cannot select it again. Changes apply at once.
data_description.messages_interval: How often the integration runs its scheduling tick (polls that are due, local queries). New messages do not wait for it: the integration reads them when the companion reports them, and also checks after 60 seconds with no messages. This sends nothing on the mesh.
data_description.expose_secrets: Off by default. Keep it off. Raw MeshCore events go to the Home Assistant event bus (meshcore_raw_event) and to MQTT brokers in raw payload mode. While this is off, the integration never forwards a private key export and replaces channel secrets with the word redacted. The integration still decrypts channel messages. Enable it only if an automation or tool needs these values. Anyone who can read your event bus or broker can then read them.

This service reads values from 'select.meshcore_recipient_type', 'select.meshcore_channel', 'select.meshcore_contact', and 'text.meshcore_message' to determine the recipient and message content. Call this service directly from a button card for a seamless messaging interface.

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The entry ID of the companion to use. If you have more than one MeshCore entry, always set it. Without it, some actions use the first entry and others refuse the call.

execute_command.name: Execute MeshCore Command
execute_command.description: Execute a command provided by the MeshCore Python library. This is an advanced feature that provides direct access to the underlying commands interface. CAUTION: Some commands will make PERMANENT CHANGES to your node's configuration. Use with care.

command.name: Command
command.description: The command with parameters to execute. Format is "[command_name] [param1] [param2] ..." Examples: - set_name "MyDevice" - send_msg "def456" "Hello from Home Assistant!" - get_bat - set_tx_power 20 - set_coords 12.345 -67.890

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The entry ID of the companion to use. If you have more than one MeshCore entry, always set it. Without it, some actions use the first entry and others refuse the call.

record_to_console.name: Record to CLI Console
record_to_console.description: Records the command and its response and fires the meshcore_cli_response event. The CLI Console sensor shows the transcript only when the CLI Console is enabled in Global Settings.

execute_command_ui.name: Execute Command from UI
execute_command_ui.description: Execute a command using the text.meshcore_command helper entity. This service reads the command from the text helper and executes it. It will automatically clear the input field after execution.

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The entry ID of the companion to use. If you have more than one MeshCore entry, always set it. Without it, some actions use the first entry and others refuse the call.

record_to_console.name: Record to CLI Console
record_to_console.description: Records the command and its response and fires the meshcore_cli_response event. The CLI Console sensor shows the transcript only when the CLI Console is enabled in Global Settings.

cli_console_clear.name: Clear CLI Console
cli_console_clear.description: Clear the CLI Console transcript. With no entry_id, clears every configured device's console.

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The config entry ID if you have multiple MeshCore devices. Leave empty to clear all.

add_selected_contact.name: Add Selected Contact
add_selected_contact.description: Add the contact selected in the discovered contact select entity to your node's contact list.

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The entry ID of the companion to use. If you have more than one MeshCore entry, always set it. Without it, some actions use the first entry and others refuse the call.

remove_selected_contact.name: Remove Selected Contact
remove_selected_contact.description: Remove the contact selected in the added contact select entity from your node's contact list.

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The entry ID of the companion to use. If you have more than one MeshCore entry, always set it. Without it, some actions use the first entry and others refuse the call.

remove_discovered_contact.name: Remove Discovered Contact
remove_discovered_contact.description: Remove a discovered contact from the discovered contacts list. This will remove the contact from Home Assistant but does NOT remove it from your node's contact list. You can specify the pubkey_prefix directly, or leave it blank to use the selected contact from the discovered contact select entity.

pubkey_prefix.name: Public Key Prefix
pubkey_prefix.description: The public key prefix of the contact to remove. It must match only one contact. Leave empty to use the selected contact from the discovered contact select entity.

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The entry ID of the companion to use. If you have more than one MeshCore entry, always set it. Without it, some actions use the first entry and others refuse the call.

cleanup_unavailable_contacts.name: Cleanup Unavailable Contacts
cleanup_unavailable_contacts.description: Remove all unavailable MeshCore contact binary sensors from Home Assistant.

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The config entry ID if you have multiple MeshCore devices. Leave empty to clean all devices.

clear_discovered_contacts.name: Clear Discovered Contacts
clear_discovered_contacts.description: Remove discovered contacts and their associated binary sensor entities from Home Assistant. When days_threshold is specified, only contacts whose last update is older than the threshold are removed and contacts saved to the node are preserved. Without days_threshold, all discovered contacts are removed. This does NOT remove contacts from your node's contact list.

days_threshold.name: Days Threshold
days_threshold.description: Only remove contacts whose last update is older than this many days. Contacts saved to the node are always preserved. If omitted, all discovered contacts are removed.

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The entry ID of the companion to use. If you have more than one MeshCore entry, always set it. Without it, some actions use the first entry and others refuse the call.

get_discovered_contact.name: Get Discovered Contact
get_discovered_contact.description: Return the full data dict for a single discovered (un-added) contact, matched by public-key prefix. In data-only mode discovered contacts have no per-contact entity, so this is the supported way to inspect one.

pubkey_prefix.name: Public Key Prefix
pubkey_prefix.description: The public key prefix (e.g. the 12-character prefix shown in the discovered-contact dropdown) of the contact to look up. A full public key also works.

entry_id.name: Config Entry ID
entry_id.description: The entry ID of the companion to use. If you have more than one MeshCore entry, always set it. Without it, some actions use the first entry and others refuse the call.

pubkey_changed.title: MeshCore public key changed
pubkey_changed.description:
The MeshCore device's public key has changed from `{old_key}...` to `{new_key}...`. All entity IDs have been automatically migrated to use the new key prefix.

If you have automations, scripts, or dashboards referencing the old entity IDs (containing `{old_key}`), you will need to update them manually to use the new prefix (`{new_key}`).

This issue can be dismissed once you have verified your configuration.
